name: L298N
description: High-voltage, high-current dual full-bridge driver that accepts standard TTL logic and drives inductive loads such as relays, solenoids, DC and stepping motors. Operates from a motor supply VS up to 46V with total DC current up to 4A, and uses a separate lower-voltage logic supply VSS so the logic works at 5V. Two enable inputs gate each bridge independently, and the lower transistor emitters of each bridge are brought out (SENSE A/B) for an external current-sense resistor. The classic high-power H-bridge, famous as the red L298N motor module.

pins.name: SENSE A
pins.description: current sensing A; connect an external sense resistor between this pin and ground (emitters of bridge A lower transistors)

pins.name: VS
pins.description: supply voltage for the power output stages (motor supply, up to 46V operating)

pins.name: ENABLE A
pins.description: enable input for bridge A (TTL; low disables bridge A)

pins.name: VSS
pins.description: logic supply voltage (typically 5V); requires a 100nF decoupling capacitor

pins.name: ENABLE B
pins.description: enable input for bridge B (TTL; low disables bridge B)

pins.name: SENSE B
pins.description: current sensing B; connect an external sense resistor between this pin and ground (emitters of bridge B lower transistors)

extra.clamp_diodes: none internal - external flyback diodes required
extra.current_sense: SENSE A / SENSE B external resistor pins

typical_application: Driving a bipolar stepper or two DC motors at higher current/voltage than a logic-IC bridge can handle, with 8 external flyback diodes.
gotchas: needs 8 EXTERNAL flyback/freewheeling diodes (fast recovery) - the L298 has NO internal clamp diodes, unlike the L293D
two separate supplies: VS (pin 4, motor power up to 46V) and VSS (pin 9, ~5V logic)
SENSE A/B pins are the bridge low-side emitters; tie to ground (directly or via a small sense resistor) - do not leave floating
the common red L298N module adds onboard flyback diodes and a 5V regulator - remove the 5V-enable jumper when VS > 12V or it can damage the regulator
high BJT saturation voltage means significant heat - a heat sink is required at higher currents
Multiwatt-15 is a single staggered inline row, not a DIP
